+## #2869 - Example case multiaxis/wrapped: a grooved bar on the A axis
+
+**Decided.** The case `examples/catalog/multiaxis/wrapped` is a 20 mm x 20 mm
+bar along X with one round-bottom ring groove at X0. Three operations use the
+catalog ball mill `BN-0600`: Rotary Offset (rough), Rotary Parallel (finish)
+and Rotary Contour (rings over the groove). The machine is the built-in
+`Tormach 770MX + microARC 4`. A setup `Wrap` selects the `Tormach PathPilot`
+post. The case test pins the three saved kinds and A motion in each posted
+section. The full regenerate and rebuild checks are in the heavy lane.
+
+**Why.**
+- The rotary kinds refuse a model that is not a shape of revolution. A groove
+  that wanders along X (a barrel cam) is refused with a message that names
+  #2772. A ring groove is a shape of revolution, and it still shows A motion in
+  each of the three kinds.
+- Rotary Parallel finishes each free end face down to the A centreline. The
+  flutes must reach the centreline from the stock radius. At radius 15 mm the
+  8 mm shank of `BN-0600` touched the end face, and verification blocked the
+  post. At radius 10 mm (stock radius 11 mm) the 15 mm flutes reach, and the
+  catalog tool works without an edit.
+- Without a setup, the post refused the program: "tilted move commands B -
+  the machine states no B rotary". With a setup on the machine's own post,
+  `Tormach PathPilot`, the program has A words only. #4422 tracks the
+  refusal without a setup. The MCP surface
+  selects a post only per setup (`set_setup_post`), so the script adds one
+  setup.
+- The rotary generators scale with the facet count. With 72 sectors and a
+  0.5 mm axial step (4176 facets), Rotary Parallel took 56 s and Rotary
+  Contour 18 s in release, past the 60 s case budget. A 30 mm bar with 48
+  sectors (1632 facets) took 17 s alone, but 59 s beside the other heavy
+  catalog cases. The final 20 mm bar with 36 sectors and a 1 mm step (1080
+  facets) and a 0.2 mm finish tolerance takes about 14 s in the parallel heavy
+  lane and about 30 s alone in debug.
+- About 30 s alone in debug is too close to the 60 s budget beside the other
+  cases of the debug suite. The `2d/slots` case (about 40 s alone) set the
+  precedent: the two full checks move to the heavy lane, and a quick test
+  pins the committed program.
+
+**Dropped.**
+- A sine (barrel-cam) groove: refused by the rotary kinds (#2772).
+- A 30 mm x 50 mm bar: the project file was 17 MB, and the shank touched the end
+  faces.
+- A 20 mm x 30 mm bar: too slow beside the other heavy catalog cases.
+- A tool edit (`flute_len` 20 mm, `shank_d` 6 mm): not needed at the smaller
+  radius.
+
+**Cost to change.** The project file is about 3.7 MB. Most of it is the Rotary
+Parallel path: its raster samples each pass about every 1.1 mm, and it steps
+the A rapids between passes. A coarser finish stepover did not make the path
+smaller. A different part or kind changes only this case folder and its test.

+# Wrapped A axis: a grooved bar
+
+This original example shows continuous 4-axis work on a round bar.
+The A axis turns during the cutting moves.
+The case uses three rotary kinds: Rotary Offset, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Contour.
+
+The model is a cylinder along X, 20 mm across and 20 mm long, from X−10 to X10.
+A round-bottom ring groove wraps once around the bar at X0.
+The groove profile is an arc of radius 5 mm, and the groove is 1.5 mm deep at its center.
+The generator checks that the mesh is closed and that each facet faces out.
+
+The built-in `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4` machine supplies the A axis along X.
+The setup `Wrap` posts with the `Tormach PathPilot` post.
+The script sets a cylinder stock along X and fits it to the model with a 1 mm margin.
+The stock is 22 mm across and 22 mm long.
+All three operations use the 6 mm ball end mill `BN-0600`, without a holder.
+
+The rotary kinds read Clearance, Retract, Top and Bottom as radii about the A axis.
+Rotary Contour is different: it reads Top and Bottom as stations along the axis.
+
+| Order | Operation | Kind | What it does |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 | Wrap rough | Rotary Offset | Removes the stock from radius 11 mm in radial levels of 1 mm and leaves 0.3 mm |
+| 2 | Wrap finish | Rotary Parallel | Passes along X and steps around the bar; it also finishes the two end faces |
+| 3 | Groove rings | Rotary Contour | Rings around the axis from X−5 to X5, over the groove |
+
+Rotary Parallel finishes each free end face down to the A centreline.
+The tool must reach the centreline from the stock radius.
+The 15 mm flutes of `BN-0600` reach past the 11 mm stock radius, so the shank stays clear.
+A thicker bar or shorter flutes make the verification report a shank collision on an end face.
+The mesh is coarse (36 sectors, 1 mm axial steps in the groove) to keep the case regeneration short.
+
+Inspect the three toolpaths in the project.
+Inspect the A words in `wrapped.nc`.
+Each operation turns A inside its cutting moves.
+The post writes a move that turns A with X, Y and Z in inverse-time feed (`G93`), then goes back to `G94`.
+A counts on past 360 degrees: Groove rings ends near A1620.
+The model mesh is embedded in `wrapped.camproj`; the project has no external model link.
+
+The rotary kinds plan contact for a shape of revolution.
+They refuse a groove that wanders along X around the bar (a barrel cam).
+Issue #2772 tracks that limit, so this case uses a ring groove.
+
+The script requires a clean verification result before it saves the project or posts the program.
+Stock simulation cannot judge a rotary program; the radial checks at generation and the gouge and collision checks still run.
+No physical CNC machine was run.
+The example has no chuck or fixture model.
+
+From the repository root, regenerate the model and rebuild the case:
+
+```sh
+python3 examples/catalog/multiaxis/wrapped/model/gen_wrapped_obj.py
+cargo xtask catalog --case multiaxis/wrapped
+```
+
+Check the catalog and its project tests:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --check
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+```
+
+The full rebuild of this case is in the heavy lane:
+
+```sh
+cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog -- catalog_multiaxis_wrapped --ignored
+```

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Provenance: original grooved cylinder: a round-bottom ring groove that wraps once about the X axis.
+"""Generate a closed cylinder along X with one wrapped ring groove."""
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+
+RADIUS = 10.0         # cylinder radius, mm
+HALF_LENGTH = 10.0    # the cylinder spans X-10 to X10
+GROOVE_X = 0.0        # the groove centre plane, x = GROOVE_X
+GROOVE_RADIUS = 5.0   # radius of the round groove profile
+GROOVE_DEPTH = 1.5    # radial depth at the groove centre
+SECTORS = 36          # 10 degree steps around the axis
+FINE = 1.0            # axial step where the groove runs
+
+
+def x_stations():
+    """Coarse steps on the plain ends, fine steps over the groove band."""
+    band = GROOVE_RADIUS + 1.0
+    fine = [GROOVE_X - band + FINE * i for i in range(int(round(2 * band / FINE)) + 1)]
+    coarse = [-HALF_LENGTH, -HALF_LENGTH + 5.0, HALF_LENGTH - 5.0, HALF_LENGTH]
+    return sorted(set(round(x, 9) for x in coarse + fine))
+
+
+def radius(x):
+    """The skin radius: the cylinder, less the round groove profile."""
+    distance = abs(x - GROOVE_X)
+    if distance >= GROOVE_RADIUS:
+        return RADIUS
+    sink = math.sqrt(GROOVE_RADIUS ** 2 - distance ** 2) - (GROOVE_RADIUS - GROOVE_DEPTH)
+    return RADIUS - max(0.0, sink)
+
+
+def point(x, j):
+    theta = 2.0 * math.pi * j / SECTORS
+    r = radius(x)
+    return (round(x, 8), round(r * math.cos(theta), 8), round(r * math.sin(theta), 8))
+
+
+def mesh():
+    xs = x_stations()
+    grid = [[point(x, j) for j in range(SECTORS)] for x in xs]
+    triangles = []
+    for i in range(len(xs) - 1):
+        for j in range(SECTORS):
+            k = (j + 1) % SECTORS
+            a, b, c, d = grid[i][j], grid[i][k], grid[i + 1][k], grid[i + 1][j]
+            # Outward normals: theta first, then +X.
+            triangles.append((a, b, c))
+            triangles.append((a, c, d))
+    low, high = (xs[0], 0.0, 0.0), (xs[-1], 0.0, 0.0)
+    for j in range(SECTORS):
+        k = (j + 1) % SECTORS
+        triangles.append((high, grid[-1][j], grid[-1][k]))
+        triangles.append((low, grid[0][k], grid[0][j]))
+    check(triangles)
+    return triangles
+
+
+def check(triangles):
+    """Every directed edge occurs once and has one reverse edge; normals face out."""
+    edges = set()
+    for tri in triangles:
+        u = [tri[1][i] - tri[0][i] for i in range(3)]
+        v = [tri[2][i] - tri[0][i] for i in range(3)]
+        n = (u[1]*v[2]-u[2]*v[1], u[2]*v[0]-u[0]*v[2], u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0])
+        if sum(c * c for c in n) < 1e-14:
+            raise ValueError("degenerate triangle")
+        centre = [sum(p[i] for p in tri) / 3.0 for i in range(3)]
+        outward = (centre[0] if abs(abs(centre[0]) - HALF_LENGTH) < 1e-9 else 0.0,
+                   centre[1], centre[2])
+        if sum(n[i] * outward[i] for i in range(3)) <= 0.0:
+            raise ValueError("inward facing triangle")
+        for edge in zip(tri, tri[1:] + tri[:1]):
+            if edge in edges:
+                raise ValueError("repeated directed edge")
+            edges.add(edge)
+    if any((q, p) not in edges for p, q in edges):
+        raise ValueError("mesh has an open edge")
+
+
+def main():
+    triangles = mesh()
+    points = sorted(set(p for tri in triangles for p in tri))
+    ids = {p: i + 1 for i, p in enumerate(points)}
+    lines = ["# Original grooved cylinder: 20 mm x 20 mm along X; "
+             "ring groove at X0, 5 mm profile radius, 1.5 mm deep."]
+    lines += ["v %.8f %.8f %.8f" % p for p in points]
+    lines += ["f " + " ".join(str(ids[p]) for p in tri) for tri in triangles]
+    out = Path(__file__).with_name("wrapped.obj")
+    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+    print(f"{out.name}: {len(points)} vertices, {len(triangles)} triangles; closed oriented mesh")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
